cohort: Pregnant women who had a live birth in New Mexico during two study epochs: pre-legalization (January 1, 2019 - March 31, 2021) and post-legalization (November 1, 2021 - November 30, 2022)
finding: Despite legalization of recreational cannabis in New Mexico, reported cannabinoid use in pregnancy decreased, but infants exposed to cannabinoids in utero continued to have lower birth weight, length, and head circumference, as well as lower Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Infants born following prenatal cannabinoid exposure were more commonly born via Cesarean section.
birth_weight: Significantly smaller birth weight in infants exposed to cannabinoids
